newsitem.title: USA: Procter & Gamble splits stock, ups dividend.
newsitem.headline: Procter & Gamble splits stock, ups dividend.

text.p: Procter & Gamble Co. on Tuesday announced a two-for-one stock split, raised its dividend and said it plans to continue repurchasing about $1 billion of its common stock through the 1997-98 fiscal year.
The consumer products giant said the stock split will be effective Aug. 22 in the form of a stock dividend. It will mail the new shares to shareholders on or after Sept. 19.
The Cincinnati-based company said the two-for-one stock split will make its market price more accessible to individual investors, which should create a broader market for its stock.
Procter & Gamble said it will continue the stock buyback programme initiated in 1995 to offset per-share earnings dilution resulting from management compensation programmes.
The company also said it expects to be able to proceed with desired strategic acquisitions in addition to the stock repurchase programme.

The company raised its annual common stock dividend to $2.02 from $1.80 per share. Its quarterly dividend was increased to 50.5 cents from 45 cents, and will be paid on Aug. 15 to stockholders of record as of July 18.
Procter & Gamble's stock rose $5.25 to $149.375 on the New York Stock Exchange.
